title: Dimensionality Reduction with Point-distributions Similarity Invariant
topic: General Machine Learning->Unsupervised and Semi-supervised Learning
claim: Existing methods yield overlapping or fragmented class structure; ours produces cleanly separated clusters, and does so with linear complexity.
layout: 2x3 grid of scatter panels, last panel is ours, lettered captions
description: Six scatter-plot panels in a 2x3 grid show 2-D embeddings of MNIST. Points are colored by digit class with a shared palette. The top row shows MDS, t-SNE and UMAP, and the caption says these have quadratic or higher complexity. MDS is a dense, mixed blob with scattered outliers. t-SNE gives large touching clusters. UMAP gives irregular clusters with some arcs and fragments. The bottom row shows PCA, an autoencoder (AE) and the proposed Ψ-DR, all with linear complexity. PCA is a heavily overlapping mass. AE collapses into a small tangle with a long blue streak. Ψ-DR, in the bottom right, shows ten compact, well-separated color clusters with white space between them. The eye goes to the sharp clusters in the last panel. Each panel is framed and captioned (a) to (f).
caption: Comparison of dimensionality reduction results on the MNIST dataset. The first row has a complexity of quadratic or higher, while the second row has linear complexity.
abstract: Existing dimensionality reduction methods all perform dimensionality reduction by preserving some invariant in the space before and after dimensionality reduction. This paper proposes a new dimensionality reduction invariant: preserving the invariant of the point-distributions similarity. We also design a linear and efficient method to achieve dimensionality reduction while preserving this invariant. We theoretically prove the feasibility of our method for dimensionality reduction. Furthermore, our results on benchmark datasets and single-cell expression data demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method.
